title: Perseus — Echoes in later ages
summary: Perseus beheaded the Gorgon Medusa using a mirrored shield and winged sandals. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Perseus beheaded the Gorgon Medusa using a mirrored shield and winged sandals. He later rescued Andromeda from a sea monster.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Perseus kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a narrative lens, Perseus is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

Myths survive by being reusable. Perseus proved endlessly reusable. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Odin and Cerberus.
